message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"3.12","text":"But if someone should wish to say that foreknowledge by way of such predictions is similar to genuinely innate foreknowledge, that person is greatly deceived. For things of this kind disclose only what is present, and that only if they speak truth. Yet in another respect even these are useful to me, for they establish that foreknowledge exists. But the foreknowledge of the one true prophet not only knows what is present but also extends its prophecy without limit as far as the future age itself, and it needs nothing for comprehension—and, of prophecies, obscure and ambiguous things, so that what is said should need another prophet for comprehension, but explicit and plain things—just as our teacher, being also a prophet, knew all things at all times through an innate and ever-flowing spirit.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τὴν διὰ τῶν τοιούτων προρρήσεων","chosen":"foreknowledge by way of such predictions","rationale":"The article introduces an implied feminine noun, most naturally πρόγνωσις from the immediate context."},{"source_quote":"ἄλλως δέ μοι καὶ αὐτὰ εὐχρηστεῖ","chosen":"Yet in another respect even these are useful to me","rationale":"ἄλλως marks another respect in which such predictions assist the argument despite not constituting genuine innate foreknowledge."},{"source_quote":"ἡ δὲ τοῦ μόνου καὶ ἀληθοῦς πρόγνωσις","chosen":"But the foreknowledge of the one true prophet","rationale":"“Prophet” is supplied from the surrounding discussion of the true prophet and from the closing comparison with the teacher as prophet. A more formally literal alternative is “the foreknowledge of the sole and true one.”"},{"source_quote":"μέχρις αὐτοῦ τοῦ μέλλοντος αἰῶνος ἀπέραντον ἐκτείνει τὴν προφητείαν","chosen":"extends its prophecy without limit as far as the future age itself","rationale":"ἀπέραντον characterizes the prophecy as unlimited, while μέχρις states that its reach extends to the future age itself."},{"source_quote":"καὶ οὐδενὸς δεῖται πρὸς ἐπίγνωσιν","chosen":"and it needs nothing for comprehension","rationale":"The genitive οὐδενός governed by δεῖται can mean “nothing” or “no one.” “No one for comprehension” is also possible, especially in view of the subsequent reference to another prophet."},{"source_quote":"καὶ προφητειῶν ἀμαυρὰ καὶ ἀμφίβολα, ἵνα ἄλλου προφήτου χρείαν ἔχῃ τὰ λεγόμενα πρὸς ἐπίγνωσιν, ἀλλὰ ῥητὰ καὶ ἁπλᾶ","chosen":"and, of prophecies, obscure and ambiguous things, so that what is said should need another prophet for comprehension, but explicit and plain things","rationale":"This deliberately preserves the printed genitive προφητειῶν, the contrasted neuter expressions, and the purpose clause without supplying an unattested predicate or extending the preceding negation. The resulting English fracture reflects the unresolved construction rather than presenting a conjectural repair as translation."},{"source_quote":"ἐνφύτῳ καὶ ἀεννάῳ πνεύματι","chosen":"through an innate and ever-flowing spirit","rationale":"The dative expresses the means by which the teacher knew. ἀένναος can mean ever-flowing, perpetual, unfailing, or unceasing; “through an innate and unceasing spirit” is an alternative."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"καὶ οὐδενὸς δεῖται πρὸς ἐπίγνωσιν, καὶ προφητειῶν ἀμαυρὰ καὶ ἀμφίβολα, ἵνα ἄλλου προφήτου χρείαν ἔχῃ τὰ λεγόμενα πρὸς ἐπίγνωσιν, ἀλλὰ ῥητὰ καὶ ἁπλᾶ","issue":"The image-checked selected reading is verified as printed, but no defensible continuous predication can presently be established. προφητειῶν is genitive plural, while ἀμαυρὰ καὶ ἀμφίβολα and ῥητὰ καὶ ἁπλᾶ are nominative or accusative neuter plurals. Attaching προφητειῶν to ἐπίγνωσιν or δεῖται still leaves the contrasted neuter expressions without a secure predicate, while treating them as objects requires an unprinted verb. The preceding οὐδενὸς is naturally governed by δεῖται and does not securely negate the following expression. The context strongly suggests that true foreknowledge does not utter obscure and ambiguous predictions requiring another prophet’s interpretation, but that intelligible sense cannot be translated from the supplied wording without supplementation. The main text therefore preserves the syntactic fracture, and the unresolved construction blocks publication.","proposed_reading":"One possible but unverified conjecture is καὶ οὐ προφητεύει ἀμαυρὰ καὶ ἀμφίβολα, ἵνα ἄλλου προφήτου χρείαν ἔχῃ τὰ λεγόμενα πρὸς ἐπίγνωσιν, ἀλλὰ ῥητὰ καὶ ἁπλᾶ (“and it does not prophesy obscure and ambiguous things, so that what is said needs another prophet for comprehension, but explicit and plain things”). This conjecture alters and supplements the selected reading and has not been substituted into the translation.","blocks_publication":true}]}]}
